Deprecated: use `metrics`, which holds the same latest values as plain
numbers.

Latest stored lifetime metrics for this social account post. Each supported
metric contains its latest snapshot, or an empty array if no observation
exists. Unsupported metrics are omitted; unsupported platforms and post
types return an empty object. Zero is a recorded value, not missing data.

info.description: This is the public-facing OpenAPI contract for WoopSocial. It supports scheduling posts for various social media platforms such as Bluesky, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, LinkedIn Pages, Pinterest, Threads, TikTok, X (formerly Twitter) and YouTube.
info.title: WoopSocial API

post.description:
Sends a short note about WoopSocial to the WoopSocial team. The note is
stored and emailed to the team.

Each organization can send a limited number of notes per day.

get.description: Returns a minimal response proving the WoopSocial API is reachable.

Returns the email of the WoopSocial user this connection acts as: the
user who approved the OAuth connection, or who created the API key.

Use it to tell which WoopSocial account a connection is signed in with.

200.description: The user this connection acts as.

get.description:
Returns media library items that belong to the API key's organization.

When `projectId` is provided, only media in that project is returned.

post.description:
Uploads a media file in a single request and creates a media item.

The server determines the media MIME type from the uploaded file.
Send a `multipart/form-data` request with the file in the `file` field.

Example:

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://api.woopsocial.com/v1/media?projectId=YOUR_PROJECT_ID' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/image.jpg'
```

Use this endpoint for straightforward uploads up to 100 MB.

For larger files, or when you need presigned part URLs, use the upload
session flow under `/media/upload-sessions`.

schema.description: Media file to upload. Maximum size is 100 MB.

post.description:
This endpoint can be used to upload both smaller and larger files (up to 5GB) in a chunked manner.
Calling this creates an upload session and returns presigned URLs for uploading the file in parts.

Upload the file in `partCount` parts, using the matching
`parts[n].uploadUrl` for each part number.

Every part except the last must be exactly `partSizeInBytes` bytes. The
last part may be smaller. After all parts have been uploaded, call
`/media/upload-sessions/{uploadSessionId}/complete` to finalize the upload
and create the media item.
post.x-woopsocial-mcp-description:
This endpoint can be used to upload both smaller and larger files (up to 5GB) in a chunked manner.
Calling this creates an upload session and returns presigned URLs for uploading the file in parts.

Upload the file in `partCount` parts by sending an HTTP PUT with the raw bytes of each part to the matching
`parts[n].uploadUrl`. Every part except the last must be exactly `partSizeInBytes` bytes. The last part may be smaller.
After all parts have been uploaded, call `media_uploads_complete_session` to finalize the upload and create the media item.
The presigned URLs expire at `expiresAt`.

Uploading the parts requires making HTTP requests yourself (for example with curl in a shell or code execution tool).
If you cannot make HTTP requests, tell the user the upload is not possible from this client.

The presigned URLs are hosted on Cloudflare R2 (`<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`).
If a network allowlist blocks the PUT, ask the user to allow `*.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`:
- claude.ai / Claude Desktop chat: Settings > Capabilities, in the code execution network settings.
- Claude Code: the sandbox's allowed network domains in settings.json.

get.description:
Returns the current status of a media upload session.

- `INITIATED`: parts can still be uploaded; the session hasn't been completed yet.
- `UPLOADED`: all parts arrived and the media item is being created. If it stays here, complete the session again.
- `READY`: the media item exists; use its `mediaId` in posts.
- `FAILED`: the upload can't be used; `failureCode` and `failureMessage` say why.
- `ABORTED`: the session can't be used anymore. Start a new one.

post.description: Call this to finalize the upload started by calling [`/media/upload-sessions`](/api-reference/media/start-media-upload-session).
post.x-woopsocial-mcp-description:
Finalizes an upload session started by `media_uploads_create_session` and creates the media item.

Call it once every part has been uploaded to its `parts[n].uploadUrl`. It returns status `READY` with the new `mediaId`, or `FAILED` with `failureCode` and `failureMessage`.
Calling it again on a finished session returns the same result.

delete.description:
Deletes one media item and its stored files.

Don't delete media that a post still waiting to publish uses.

post.description:
Creates a (parent) post with one or more social account (child) posts.

All referenced social accounts must belong to the same project.

The request is validated atomically. If any social account fails validation, the post is not created.

Validates a post without creating one.

This endpoint applies the same validation rules as [`POST /posts`](/api-reference/posts/create-post),
including social account resolution, platform-specific validation, and
media validation for referenced media library items.

This tool applies the same validation rules as `posts_create`,
including social account resolution, platform-specific validation, and
media validation for referenced media library items.

delete.description:
Deletes one scheduled post by post ID.

A post can only be deleted when all of its social account deliveries are
still `NOT_STARTED`.

409.description: Post cannot be deleted in its current state.

get.description:
Returns one post with its social account posts inline: one per
target social account, each with its own `deliveryStatus`.

Use it after creating a post to see whether each target was published.
Returns projects that belong to the same organization as the API key. A project corresponds to a "Business Profile" in the UI.

200.description: Projects available for media upload and post creation.

post.description:
Creates a project in the API key's organization.

Use projects to isolate social accounts, media, and posts for a
specific user, client, or brand in your application.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes one project and its related data, including
connected social accounts, OAuth grants, media references, and posts.

get.description:
Returns standalone social account posts for the API key's organization.

Each item includes the content, schedule, delivery status and latest stored analytics for a given social account target.

Returns the organization's social account posts published in a range of
UTC days, each with its latest stored metrics. Posts are ordered by
`sortBy`, highest first, or newest first when `sortBy` is omitted.

Metrics are lifetime totals since publishing, as of
`metricsCollectedAt`. They are collected about once a day, and reading
them does not refresh them.

What `views` counts by platform:
- `INSTAGRAM`, `FACEBOOK`, `THREADS`: times the post was shown, repeats included.
- `TIKTOK`, `YOUTUBE`: video plays.
- `PINTEREST`: video views. Image Pins have none.
- `LINKEDIN_PAGES` reports `impressions` and `uniqueImpressions` instead.

parameters.description: First UTC day of the publish range, inclusive.
parameters.name: startDate

parameters.description: Last UTC day of the publish range, inclusive. The range can span at most 366 days.
parameters.name: endDate

parameters.description: Metric to order the posts by, highest first. Posts without it come last.
parameters.name: sortBy

delete.description: Deletes one social account post by ID.

get.description:
Returns social accounts that can currently be used for publishing.

When `projectId` is provided, only social accounts usable within that project are returned.

post.description:
Generates a browser authorization URL for connecting a new social account to a project.

This endpoint is useful for multi-user integrations where your application lets
your own users, clients, or brands connect their social accounts to WoopSocial
without giving them access to your WoopSocial account.

A common flow is:
1. Create or select a WoopSocial project for your user, client, or brand.
2. Call this endpoint from your backend with that `projectId`, the target `platform`,
   and a `redirectUrl` in your application.
3. Open the returned `url` in your user's browser.
4. After OAuth completes, WoopSocial redirects the browser back to `redirectUrl`
   with result query parameters.
5. Use `projectId` and `socialAccountIds` from the redirect, or call
   [`GET /social-accounts?projectId=...`](/api-reference/social-accounts/list-social-accounts),
   to store or confirm the connected account in your application.

When `redirectUrl` is provided, the browser is redirected back to that URL after
the OAuth callback is handled.

For Facebook, WoopSocial shows a page-selection screen after authorization
because Facebook may return more pages than the user appeared to select in
the Facebook dialog in cases where the user has authorized with WoopSocial previously. The selected pages are connected to the single
`projectId` from this request, then WoopSocial redirects back to
`redirectUrl` when one was provided.

When `redirectUrl` is provided, WoopSocial appends these query parameters on success:
- `status=success`
- `projectId`: the project identifier from the request
- `platform`: the connected social platform
- `socialAccountIds`: comma-separated connected social account identifiers. This may contain one or more IDs depending on the platform OAuth flow.

When `redirectUrl` is provided, WoopSocial appends these query parameters on failure:
- `status=error`
- `projectId`: the project identifier from the request
- `platform`: the requested social platform
- `error`: an OAuth callback error code

If the OAuth callback state is missing or expired, WoopSocial cannot safely
determine the original `redirectUrl`, so the callback returns an HTTP error
instead of redirecting.

The redirect never includes OAuth tokens or credentials.
post.x-woopsocial-mcp-description:
Generates a browser authorization URL for connecting a new social account to a project.

Flow:
1. Call this tool with the `projectId` and target `platform`. Omit `redirectUrl` unless the user asks for one.
2. Give the returned `url` to the user and ask them to open it in their browser and complete the authorization.
3. Once the user says they are done, call `social_accounts_list` with the `projectId` to confirm the connected account.

For Facebook, WoopSocial shows a page-selection screen after authorization. The selected pages are connected to the `projectId`.

delete.description:
Deletes one social account connection by ID.

This removes the associated OAuth grant, including stored access and
refresh tokens, so the account no longer counts toward the
organization's active connected-account allowance.

get.description:
Returns account-level metrics of one social account over a range of UTC
days: its follower count and the views, engagements and other activity
across all of its content. Per-post metrics are in each social account
post's `metrics`.

Each point covers one UTC day. Metrics are collected about once a day,
so the latest day or two may be missing. Reading analytics does not
refresh them.

Metrics by platform:
- `FACEBOOK`: followers, views, engagements.
- `INSTAGRAM`: followers, views, engagements, likes, comments, shares, saves.
- `LINKEDIN_PAGES`: followers, impressions, engagements, likes, comments, shares, clicks.
- `PINTEREST`: followers, impressions, engagements, saves, clicks, views (video views).
- `YOUTUBE`: followers (subscribers), views, likes, comments, shares.
- `TIKTOK`: followers, views, likes, comments, shares. Only accounts
  connected through the TikTok for Business app collect them.
- `THREADS`: followers, likes, comments (replies), shares (reposts and
  quotes), clicks. Followers start on the day the account is first
  collected, since Threads reports no follower history.
- Other platforms have no account analytics and return empty `metrics`.

parameters.description: First UTC day of the range, inclusive.
parameters.name: startDate

parameters.description: Last UTC day of the range, inclusive. The range can span at most 366 days.
parameters.name: endDate

get.description:
Returns platform-specific input options for a connected social account.

Use this endpoint to discover valid values for flattened post-target
fields such as `pinterestBoardId` and `privacyLevel`.
Returns all registered webhook endpoints for the organization. The `signingSecret` field is omitted.

post.description:
Registers a URL to receive webhook events for the specified event types.

The response includes a `signingSecret` (base64-encoded, 32 bytes) that is
returned **once only**. Use it to verify the `X-Woop-Signature` header on
incoming webhook payloads.

**Signature format:** `t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256-hex>`
**Signed payload:** `<unix>.<json-body>`

422.description: Validation error (unknown event type, empty url, etc.).

delete.description:
Deletes one webhook endpoint, so its URL stops receiving events.

To receive events again, register the URL anew. The new endpoint gets
a new `signingSecret`.

parameters.description: The `id` of a webhook endpoint from List webhook endpoints.
parameters.name: webhookId
